title: Rebuilding a Field's Open-Problem Catalog from the Literature: A Two-Layer Knowledge Graph, and Why Status Must Stay Proposed
abstract: arXiv:2610.39641v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A research field records its open problems in surveys, keynotes and community reports. Those are prose, written every few years, and nobody can ask them who works on a problem now or whether it was settled last year. We argue the problems should be data, and we build the system that makes them so: a hand-curated problem layer carried in unchanged, under an evidence layer rebuilt from a bibliographic index, joined by typed, provenance-carrying links in one graph database and queryable from one language. A language model does four jobs -- per-paper extraction, catalog grounding, per-paper status verdict, and idea generation -- each constrained to a candidate set so out-of-set answers are refused rather than stored. We report a study on two curated catalogs, database research (1,053 problems) and AI research (1,000 problems), each with a prior catalog-only graph. The rebuilt graph answers every question the catalog-only graph answered --

translated_title: 从文献中重建领域的开放问题目录：双层知识图谱，以及为什么问题状态必须保持为“待解决”
translated_abstract: 一个研究领域通过综述文章、主题演讲和社区报告来记录其开放问题。这些都是散文式的文字，每隔几年才写一次，而且没有人能向它们提问：现在是谁在研究某个问题？它去年是否已经被解决了？我们认为这些问题应当成为数据，并构建了使其成为数据的系统：一个经过人工整理的问题层被原封不动地保留，其下方是一个从文献索引重建的证据层，两层之间通过携带类型和溯源信息的链接相连接，存放在同一个图数据库中，并可以用同一种查询语言进行查询。语言模型承担四项工作——逐篇论文抽取、目录对齐、逐篇论文状态判定以及想法生成——每一项任务都被约束在候选集合之内，因此集合之外的答案会被拒绝而不是被存储。我们报告了一项针对两个经人工整理目录的研究：数据库研究领域（1,053个问题）和人工智能研究领域（1,000个问题），每个领域都有一个先前的仅含目录的图谱。重建后的图谱能够回答仅含目录的图谱所能回答的所有问题——（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文构建了一个双层知识图谱，把领域的开放问题从散文式目录变成可查询的数据——人工整理的问题层保持不变，证据层从文献索引重建并由带溯源信息的类型化链接相连，语言模型的抽取、对齐、状态判定与想法生成四项任务均被约束在候选集合内以拒绝集外答案，并论证问题状态必须始终保持“待解决”而不能被自动判定为已解决。
en_tdlr: This paper turns a field's open problems into queryable data via a two-layer knowledge graph—an unchanged hand-curated problem layer over an evidence layer rebuilt from a bibliographic index, joined by typed, provenance-carrying links—with a language model whose four tasks (per-paper extraction, catalog grounding, status verdicts, and idea generation) are constrained to candidate sets, and argues that problem status must stay "proposed" rather than be automatically marked as solved.
